claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me first review the official eligibility rules to ensure I can give you accurate guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I've reviewed the Child Benefit eligibility rules. To help determine if you're eligible, I need to ask you some questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17, I need to understand their education or training status, as this affects eligibility for Child Benefit.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - doing A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I need to confirm a few more details:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - in Manchester actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

Does Alex work for 24 hours or more per week, or do they receive any benefits in their own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work that much - just focuses on studies really. And no, they don't get any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 17 years old and in approved education (A-levels), which means they qualify under the rules for children aged 16-19 who remain in approved education or training
- You live with Alex in the UK (Manchester) and are responsible for them
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week or receive benefits in their own right

All the eligibility criteria are met, so you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. However, this doesn't affect your eligibility to claim - you can still receive Child Benefit.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If Alex's circumstances change (for example, if they leave education, start working 24+ hours per week, or start receiving benefits), you'll need to inform HMRC as this may affect your entitlement.
